core_themes.name: Productivity and infrastructure
core_themes.claim: The UK has long lagged other advanced economies on productivity, and infrastructure investment raises productivity and thereby wages and living standards.

core_themes.name: Local authority role and borrowing costs
core_themes.claim: Local authorities are responsible for a sizeable share of infrastructure investment and are best placed to know local needs, but high borrowing costs could prevent them from delivering needed projects.

core_themes.name: Local government borrowing landscape
core_themes.claim: Local authorities borrow mainly via the PWLB at existing standard, certainty and project rates (about 75% of borrowing), in a debt market that is evolving with new lenders.

diagnosis.note: Evidence on the scale of the borrowing-cost barrier is asserted rather than quantified; the diagnosis mixes the national productivity problem with the local financing problem.

core_themes.name: Discounted Local Infrastructure Rate
core_themes.claim: The government proposes up to £1 billion of lending to local authorities at gilts + 60 basis points for high value-for-money projects, because cheaper borrowing will make it easier to finance infrastructure that raises productivity.

core_themes.name: Complementing wider infrastructure funding
core_themes.claim: The new rate fits alongside rising central government infrastructure investment, the Housing Infrastructure Fund and Growth Deals, giving local authorities additional financing options.

core_themes.name: Expected impacts
core_themes.claim: The government expects significant take-up that would raise infrastructure investment, productive capacity, business conditions and household living standards, with some risk of crowding out private finance or shifting local spending.

proposal.note: No alternative options are discussed and no evidence from the earlier project rate is offered; the impact assessment is asserted and the policy is still subject to consultation.

core_themes.name: Delivery through the PWLB
core_themes.claim: The rate would be delivered via the PWLB, or its successor, using the existing statutory lending machinery, with no expected extra administrative cost, for a three-year window and loans of up to 50 years.

core_themes.name: Competitive bid and appraisal process
core_themes.claim: Allocations would be awarded to council bids that show high value for money through Green Book-style appraisal (net present value, business case, risk assessment) signed off by the Section 151 Officer, with details to be set out later.

core_themes.name: Eligibility and scope limits
core_themes.claim: Eligible bodies and sectors are defined, the £1 billion is capped, and the rate is restricted to approved projects and not available for refinancing, keeping accountability with democratically accountable councils.

implementation.note: Details of the bidding process are explicitly left to be set out in due course; the consultation questions ask only about impacts, not about delivery design.
